judge_ground_0.evidence: Static trace of captured head a8abe0c43 against base 4dabf06ef; no live reproduction or timing-frequency claim. The relevant control/helper/recovery/selection files are new in this diff. control.rs finish sets cleanup_done before finish_process, so Drop cannot retry. A permitted execution is try_wait -> Ok(None), then descheduling while the killed child exits, then resumption after the cleanup deadline: lines 221-222 return without another try_wait, and the owned Child is discarded. Repository-wide src search for SIGCHLD, waitpid, waitid, SA_NOCLDWAIT and reaper found no production global child reaper; the test-support reaper is not such a mechanism. Official Rust documentation fetched at https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/process/struct.Child.html states: 'The standard library does not automatically wait on child processes (not even if the Child is dropped)'. It also documents that Unix try_wait reaps an exited process. Official Linux proc documentation fetched at https://docs.kernel.org/filesystems/proc.html documents zombie process state, UID, process group and start_time ('time the process started after system boot'). helper.rs birth/leader_at reads start and UID but ignores state, so this unreaped same-birth child continues to classify Same; classify cannot return Quiescent for Same regardless of the group probe result. queue_recovery.rs only reconciles Quiescent and never reaps; store/wake_intents.rs UNRESOLVED includes cleanup_quarantined=1 independently of logical fulfillment, and selection.rs fences both transports when native_no_add_exception=0. findings.claim: A helper that is not reaped before the 250 ms cleanup deadline is abandoned as a child, leaving its wake scope permanently quarantined for the lifetime of the daemon even after the helper exits.
findings.evidence: finish_process returns at lines 221-222 even when reaped is false; this occurs when SIGKILL completion is delayed, or the daemon is descheduled between try_wait and the deadline check. finish sets cleanup_done=true before attempting cleanup (line 163), so Peer::drop never retries; the Child is dropped without being handed to a reaper. Repository search finds no production SIGCHLD handler or waitpid reaper. The exited direct child consequently remains a zombie. helper.rs leader_at checks only birth identity and UID, without treating zombie state specially, so the retained PID/start still yields Same; classify requires Ended plus absent group to clear quarantine. QueueRecovery therefore cannot reconcile this helper, and selection.rs blockers keeps both transports fenced while cleanup_quarantined=1, including after logical fulfillment. This is a long-running daemon path: a transient cleanup scheduling delay becomes persistent loss of wake availability until daemon restart, rather than merely the intended temporary conservative quarantine. Static control-flow review; no live reproduction was run.
